# google_cloud_identity_inbound_sso_assignment

Assigns an inbound SSO behavior (SSO off, a SAML SSO profile or an OIDC SSO profile) to a
Google Group or an Org Unit of a Google enterprise customer.

The caller must be a Google Workspace / Cloud Identity administrator of the
customer with the SSO settings privilege (for example a super admin);
Google Cloud IAM roles are not sufficient.

If you are using User ADCs (Application Default Credentials) with this resource,
you must specify a `billing_project` and set `user_project_override` to true
in the provider configuration. Otherwise the Cloud Identity API will return a 403 error.
Your account must have the `serviceusage.services.use` permission on the
`billing_project` you defined.


To get more information about InboundSsoAssignment, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/identity/docs/reference/rest/v1/inboundSsoAssignments)
* How-to Guides
    * [Assign SSO profiles](https://cloud.google.com/identity/docs/how-to/assign-sso-profiles)


## Example Usage - Cloud Identity Inbound Sso Assignment Group Saml


```hcl
resource "google_cloud_identity_group" "group" {
  display_name         = "sso-group"
  initial_group_config = "WITH_INITIAL_OWNER"
  parent               = "customers/A01b123xz"

  group_key {
    id = "sso-group@example.com"
  }

  labels = {
    "cloudidentity.googleapis.com/groups.discussion_forum" = ""
  }
}

resource "google_cloud_identity_inbound_saml_sso_profile" "saml_profile" {
  customer     = "customers/A01b123xz"
  display_name = "saml-profile"

  idp_config {
    entity_id                  = "https://idp.example.com/saml-profile"
    single_sign_on_service_uri = "https://idp.example.com/sso"
  }
}

resource "google_cloud_identity_inbound_sso_assignment" "assignment" {
  customer     = "customers/A01b123xz"
  target_group = google_cloud_identity_group.group.name
  rank         = 1
  sso_mode     = "SAML_SSO"

  saml_sso_info {
    inbound_saml_sso_profile = google_cloud_identity_inbound_saml_sso_profile.saml_profile.name
  }

  sign_in_behavior {
    redirect_condition = "NEVER"
  }
}
```

## Example Usage - Cloud Identity Inbound Sso Assignment Org Unit


```hcl
resource "google_cloud_identity_inbound_sso_assignment" "assignment" {
  customer        = "customers/A01b123xz"
  target_org_unit = "orgUnits/03abcxyz"
  sso_mode        = "SSO_OFF"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `sso_mode` -
  (Required)
  Inbound SSO behavior.
  Possible values are: `SSO_OFF`, `SAML_SSO`, `OIDC_SSO`, `DOMAIN_WIDE_SAML_IF_ENABLED`.


* `customer` -
  (Optional)
  The customer. For example: `customers/C0123abc`. If omitted, the customer of the caller is used.

* `target_group` -
  (Optional)
  The Google Group to assign. Must be of the form `groups/{group}`.

* `target_org_unit` -
  (Optional)
  The Org Unit to assign. Must be of the form `orgUnits/{org_unit}`.

* `rank` -
  (Optional)
  Must be zero (which is the default value so it can be omitted) for assignments with
  `target_org_unit` set and must be greater-than-or-equal-to one for assignments with
  `target_group` set.

* `saml_sso_info` -
  (Optional)
  SAML SSO details. Must be set if and only if `sso_mode` is set to `SAML_SSO`.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_saml_sso_info).

* `oidc_sso_info` -
  (Optional)
  OpenID Connect SSO details. Must be set if and only if `sso_mode` is set to `OIDC_SSO`.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_oidc_sso_info).

* `sign_in_behavior` -
  (Optional)
  Assertions about users assigned to an IdP will always be accepted from that IdP. This
  controls whether/when Google should redirect a user to the IdP. Unset (defaults) is the
  recommended configuration.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_sign_in_behavior).

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_saml_sso_info"></a>The `saml_sso_info` block supports:

* `inbound_saml_sso_profile` -
  (Required)
  Name of the `InboundSamlSsoProfile` to use. Must be of the form
  `inboundSamlSsoProfiles/{inbound_saml_sso_profile}`.

<a name="nested_oidc_sso_info"></a>The `oidc_sso_info` block supports:

* `inbound_oidc_sso_profile` -
  (Required)
  Name of the `InboundOidcSsoProfile` to use. Must be of the form
  `inboundOidcSsoProfiles/{inbound_oidc_sso_profile}`.

<a name="nested_sign_in_behavior"></a>The `sign_in_behavior` block supports:

* `redirect_condition` -
  (Optional)
  When to redirect sign-ins to the IdP. Unset means "always".
  Possible values are: `NEVER`.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `inboundSsoAssignments/{{inbound_sso_assignment_id}}`

* `name` -
  Resource name of the Inbound SSO Assignment.
  Format: `inboundSsoAssignments/{inbound_sso_assignment_id}`.

* `inbound_sso_assignment_id` -
  The server-assigned ID of the Inbound SSO Assignment (the last segment of `name`).

## Import


InboundSsoAssignment can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `inboundSsoAssignments/{{inbound_sso_assignment_id}}`
* `{{inbound_sso_assignment_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import InboundSsoAssignment using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    inboundSsoAssignmentId = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_cloud_identity_inbound_sso_assignment.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import InboundSsoAssignment using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "inboundSsoAssignments/{{inbound_sso_assignment_id}}"
  to = google_cloud_identity_inbound_sso_assignment.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), InboundSsoAssignment can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_cloud_identity_inbound_sso_assignment.default inboundSsoAssignments/{{inbound_sso_assignment_id}}
$ terraform import google_cloud_identity_inbound_sso_assignment.default {{inbound_sso_assignment_id}}
```
